properties.parkdesc: Frogtown Community Center is home to a wide variety of programs and activities. Horseshoe courts can be found just north of the center on Como Ave.
With its rolling hills and old oak trees, this 10-acre plot is a great place to have a summer picnic, or to sit under a tree and read a book.
The Griggs Recreation Center site has recently been renovated as of fall 2014. The site received a new large, nature-themed play area as well as new walkways and landscaping.
Hayden Heights is a City operated recreation center offering a wide range of activities and programs.

Prosperity Park, along with Prosperity Heights Park to the south, combine to provide Saint Paul's East Side with a large expanse of recreational and natural green space to utilize, including a playground, softball field, tennis courts, and a picnic area.

Tucked in the northeast corner of Saint Paul, Frost Lake Park is comprised mainly of Frost Lake and surrounding trees and trails. The Frost Lake Recreation Center has been repartnered with Saint Paul Public Schools.
Weida Park's features a rectangular, lit field perfect for games of soccer, Ultimate Frisbee, lacrosse, and more. The park also contains a basketball court, picnic tables, and a playground area.
Hamm Park displays well-groomed and colorful flowers, trees, and bushes throughout the year and sits kitty corner from Swede Hollow Park. Visitors will find trails connecting the two locations.
Margaret Park contains many amenities that encourage residents to stay active including a playground, vast open space, and a winter sledding hill.
Skidmore Park is well known to locals for its beautiful and well-stocked community garden. The park brings together neighbors with events and educates families on sustainability.
Parks Maintenance Area
Daytons Bluff is a city operated recreation center offering a wide range of activities and programs.
Wilder Recreation Center offers a football field, softball field, playground and a gym. City Academy High School is located within Wilder Recreation Center.
Sackett Park provides nearly 14 acres of recreational space for baseball and softball games as well as small soccer games under the lights.
Tilden Park is a popular location for families to gather due to its comfortable size, open space, ample seating, and plentiful playground equipment.
The park has a covered band shell with electricity, many gardens, and a beautiful stream running diagonally through the park.
Budding area athletes have the opportunity to play ball and soccer under the lights at Sylvan Park.
Where the new Trout Brook Regional Trail and the popular Gateway State Trail meet, visitors will find Cayuga Park, which features horseshoes, a picnic area, and a soon to be remodled play area.

A small neighborhood park east of Pig's Eye Lake, Taylor Park offers visitors an open green space perfect for pick-up games, a playground for children to play on, and picnic tables for families to gather around.

Lewis Park draws many families in throughout the year looking for a safe and spacious place to bring children to play. The park features picnic areas, trails, and open spaces suitable for small activities and games. The most popular feature, a tot lot constructed in 2008, provides peace of mind to parents and guardians with its synthetic turf surfacing and child-friendly equipment. A splash pad, Saint Paul's first, also provides entertainment and relief during the summer.
Hamm Memorial Plaza is a small, circular downtown park.
Near the heart of downtown, Capital Centre Plaza is a popular location for those looking for a bench to eat lunch at.
The park features a beautiful fountain and is surrounded by the Saint Paul Hotel, Landmark Center, Ordway and the Downtown Library.

Irvine park is one of the most popular outdoor wedding locations, nestled in a quiet, shady residential neighborhood in a historic district just west of downtown Saint Paul. Irvine Park features include a gazebo with electrical outlets that holds approximately 10 people, and an ornate fountain that serves as the park's focal point.
Two playgrounds, a picnic area, and open green space highlight Ryan Park's recreational opportunities for visitors.

Groups visiting Carty Park will find plenty of picnic tables as well as a two playground areas on the park's eastern half. A half-court basketball court and two tennis courts occupy the remaining half.
MLK Recreation Center is a city operated recreation center offering a wide variety of activities and programs.
Tatum Park is home to the Tatum Park Community Garden. Local volunteers help to run the garden throughout the year, planting perennials and edibles on a rotating basis.
Cato Park is a mounded traffic island.

Visitors to Ames Lake Park will find a beautifully designed pier curving into Ames Lake. After a few laps, walkers, runners, bicyclists, and more will find easy access to the Bruce Vento Regional Trail and Phalen Regional Park for extended activity.

Visitors to Eastside Heritage Park will find a large open green area suitable for games of football, soccer, ultimate frisbee, and more. The 9-acre park also contains a shelter and restroom facilities, making it an ideal place for family gathering.
Wacouta Commons is a downtown park with open space and a playground.
Eagle Street Plaza, located at Chestnut Street and Ryan Avenue, is a small downtown park featuring a Charlie Brown statue.
South of Holman Field, Concord Park is a largely undeveloped strip of land packed densely with vegetation.

High Bridge Park North is home to one of Saint Paul's more unique pieces of public art. Stone Watcher, created in 1995, sits in the middle of a circular path, providing views of the bound boulders from every angle.

A spectacular view of downtown Saint Paul and zero through traffic make Prospect Park a unique getaway for families and those looking to play and relax. A playground and ample seating via benches and picnic tables round out the experience.

The perfect compliment to the historic Landmark Center, Landmark Plaza beautifies downtown Saint Paul with vibrant green lawns and scene-setting trees. In the winter, Landmark Plaza is home to the Winter Skate refrigerated ice rink, a free skating rink.
Bohland Triangle is one of several traffic islands in Saint Paul. This mini park helps to create a sense of open space for local residents.
Valley Park provides visitors with a nearly 13-acre open field for large group activities and games such as softball, football, soccer, and more.
The Highland Park Community Center is the new name for the partnership between the former Hillcrest Recreation Center and Highland Park Library, which have been recently renovated and expanded.
This park offers many recreational opportunities such as horseshoes, tennis, and softball.
West Minnehaha is a City operated recreation center offering a wide variety of activities and programs.
Terrace Park provides visitors an opportunity to ascend the bluffs via a stairway.
Bluff Park is a natural formation of elevated land densely packed with trees. The park contributes to the beautiful urban canopy across all of Saint Paul.
Desnoyer Park contains every amenity needed for a successful outing: a softball field complete with lights, a playground, a tennis court, a half-court basketball court and a seasonal soccer field.
Pelham Triangle is quarter-of-an-acre mini park that sits a couple blocks south of Desnoyer Park.
Located just outside of the Cathedral of Saint Paul, Summit Park contains one of the city's most noticeable and notable monuments, Soldiers and Sailors Monument.
Boyd Park is well visited by many residents of the Cathedral Hill neighborhood. Bike racks, paved sidewalks, and a fully outfitted playground make for an accessible, enjoyable time outside.
Cathedral Hill Park is the perfect welcoming space for visitors to the Cathedral of Saint Paul.
Visitors to McQuillan Park will find plenty of shading while playing tennis or tag. The park is centrally located in Saint Paul's Cathedral Hill neighborhood.
The Holly Park tot lot contains friendly equipment such as a small swing set, a sand pit, and a small slide.
Visitors will notice beautifully groomed gardens and bushes near the statue. A wide open lawn also provides opportunities for small games and activities.
Summit Overlook is home to a statue known as New York Eagle.
Point of View Park is a small park that overlooks the West Seventh neighborhood from its position opposite of I-35E.
One of several traffic islands in Saint Paul, this mini park helps to create a sense of open space for local residents.

Dousman Park's small playground is perfect for parents with small toddlers wanting to get out and play. A nearby bench and picnic table as well as plenty of shade from trees provides provide opportunities to sit back and enjoy the day.
Edgcumbe Recreation Center is a City of Saint Paul facility with year round recreation opportunities.
Duluth and Case is a city operated recreation center offer a wide range of activities and programs.
In addition to the baseball field, two tennis courts, basketball court, soccer field, picnic area and a dog park, Arlington/Arkwright Park will also feature a skate park as of spring 2015.
Holcombe Circle is a traffic island bordering the northeast corner of Webster Park.
North End Community Center is a City operated recreation center and home to a wide variety of programs and activities.
Oxford Community Center, also known as Jimmy Lee Recreation Center, is home an aquatic center, a large synthetic field for a variety of sports, and many other programs and activities.

Arlington Hills Community Center is a joint facility run by Saint Paul Parks and Recreation and the Saint Paul Public Library. Officially open in May of 2014, the community center offers a variety of open spaces for the public to utilize for parties, meetings, and more. Community members are also able to take advantage of the many learning opportunities afforded by the library, learning lab, and Createch Studio, a technology-specific, creative space for youth.
Dedicated to the public in 1886, Fountain Park is a half-acre, triangular plot of land northeast of Highland Park.
Thought it may appear like a private property, the triangular strip of land at the intersection of Howell Avenue and Edgecumb Road is in fact a 3/4 acre public park.

Nestled in the middle of dozens of surrounding houses, Dawson Park has remained an integral piece to Saint Paul's urban canopy over the years. The undeveloped plot of land, measured at nearly 2 acres, is one of several natural preserves in the city,
Walsh Park is a secluded park east of Highland Park. It joins nearby Dawson Park as preserve meant to maintain the natural growth of the area.
Maryland Avenue Open Space is a preserve consisting of a wooded, marshy area just blocks from the border of Saint Paul and Maplewood near Beaver Lake.
North Dale Recreation Center has a variety of programs and athletic facilities, including a refrigerated hockey rink during winter months.
City operated recreation center offering a wide range of activities and programs.
Stinson Park contains open green space suitable for small activities and a new playground is projected to be completed in 2014.

Accessible from the Fairview Avenue stop along the Green Line, Iris Park contains one of the City's most beautiful artificial ponds. The park also offers a picnic area and much-needed green space along University Avenue for residents to use and enjoy.
Just west of Langford Park, Gordon Square flourishes with beautiful flowers and plants.
Clayland Park, adjacent to Newell Park, holds two tennis courts and provides open green space for small activities.
Xinia Triangle is a traffic island.
Willow Reserve is an undeveloped nature preserve on Saint Paul's North End.
Amenities at Marydale Park include picnic tables, grills, a tot-lot, fishing pier, and a trail surrounding Loeb Lake.

Visitors to Cochran Park will immediately notice its primary attraction, a bronze sculpture known as "Indian Hunter and His Dog," in the middle of a flowery fountain. Nearby, visitors can take in the view of the sculpture while sitting inside a small brick structure with seating for several individuals.
Wedged between Ramsey County Government Center East and Kellogg Park, the half-acre Culture Park contains a cozy sitting area, outfitted with artistic landscaping, overlooking the Mississippi River.
Located in downtown Saint Paul, Kellogg Park features two fountains and an arbor. This park offers a great view of the Mississippi River.

Highwood Hills Park is located on Saint Paul's East Side and is adjacent to Highwood Hills Elementary School. The park contains a small picnic area, soccer field, playground, two half-court basketball courts, and a full-court basketball court. Field reservations can be made by contacting Battle Creek Recreation Center.
Hancock Recreation Center is a City operated recreation center with a wide variety of programs and activities.
Northwest Como is a City of Saint Paul recreation center home to many activities, programs, and athletic facilities.
Visitors are treated to stunning views of the State Capital, Cathedral of Saint Paul, the Mississippi River, and downtown Saint Paul.
El Rio Vista is a city operated recreation center offering a wide range of activities and programs and featuring the newly renovated Twins All-Star Park at Gilbert de la O Field.
McDonough Recreation Center is a city operated recreation center offering a wide variety of activities and programs.
Donated by the Pedro family, this downtown plot of land is currently the site of the "Urban Flower Field" project and will eventually be developed into a permanent park.

An ideal location for a short afternoon stroll, Homecroft Park contains a horseshoe court, two tennis courts and a tennis practice board. The adjacent Homecroft Recreation Center, which contains a playground, basketball court, two softball fields, picnic area, and soccer field, has been repartnered with Saint Paul Public Schools.
Bluff Preservation Area is a nature preserve contributing to Saint Paul's beautiful urban canopy.
Scenic overlooks and recreational opportunities abound at Cherokee Regional Park.
Dickerman Park spans a quarter mile along University Avenue and the Green Line train.

The southern triangle features a small play area equipped with a slide, a swing-set, and a dome climber. Those looking for open space will find the northern triangle suitable for small group activities and games.
Located alongside Snelling Avenue, Hamline Park contains a variety of amenities for visitors to use.
Horton Park has several picnic tables as well as a mini arboretum.
More triangle than square, Cromwell Square is a pleasant patch of green space north of Hampden Park.
This West Side mini park contains a playground and picnic facilities.
Just west of Macalester College, Cambridge Triangle occupies a 0.07 acre plot of land at the intersection of Cambridge Street, Amherst Street, and Princeton Avenue.
City of Saint Paul Recreation Center.

A popular neighborhood park among locals, Mattocks Park has a little bit of everything for everyone. Two tennis courts, a half-court basketball court, and a playground and tot-lot can be found on the western half of the park.
Lockwood Park is a popular park among locals due to its large, flat errain. The park can be utilized for football, soccer, and softball as well as play time for children in the large playground area.
The Sanneh Foundation is running many different types of programs from Conway Recreation Center. These programs include open basketball, futsal, after school computer time, and much more.
Burns Avenue Park provides visitors with plenty of recreational opportunities including a tennis court, half-court basketball court, and a new playground.
Palace Recreation Center offers a variety of activities and athletic facilities, including a refrigerated hockey rink in the winter.
Linwood is a City operated recreation center offering a wide variety of activities and programs.
Merriam Park Recreation Center is a city operated recreation center offering a wide variety of activities and programs.
May Park is a rectangular park with open space, a playground, and picnic area.
Lyton Park contains two of Saint Paul's more whimsical sculptures: Girl on Dolphin and Boy on Turtle.
The eastern half of Front Park contains a baseball field and two softball fields while the western half contains a newly renovated skate park.

Located just west of the Minnesota State Fairgrounds, Alden Square Park is anything but a square. The triangular plot of land is perfect for spontaneous picnics and spacious enough to toss around a baseball.

Within College Park, visitors will find two tennis courts, a basketball court, and playground equipment for dozens of children to use at a time. The remaining 4+ acres make for a perfect spot for a game of capture the flag.

Kenwood Park is one of only a few parks in Saint Paul completely surrounded by brick roads. The mini park, at less than one-fifth of an acre, functions as the center island of a cul-de-sac for nearby homes overlooking I-35E.
Crocus Hill Terrace Park overlooks I-35E and contributes to Saint Paul's beautiful urban canopy with its densely packed trees.
Situated just south of Harriet Island Regional Park and east of Cherokee Regional Park, Alice Park provides a half-acre of land for local residents to use.

Among the many opportunities Baker Recreation Center offers are a playground, baseball field, tennis courts, and seasonal sledding hill. The Baker Recreation Center building has been repartnered with Saint Paul Public Schools.
Belvidere Park borders the West Side Boys & Girls Club and sports two softball fields, a baseball field, and a soccer field.
Raymond Square is a traffic island that functions as an extension of neighboring Hampden Park.
Renovated in 2013, Hampden Park was redesigned to provide the safest and most open experience possible for visitors.
Oakley Square acts as a buffer between traffic on Lynnhurst Avenue West and Iris Park's northwest side.

Just south of Lake Phalen, Lane Place Park is a one-acre stretch of green space available for general use. Though the park is dotted with trees, patches of open space do provide opportunities for small activities and games.
Van Slyke Triangle is perhaps Saint Paul's most unique traffic island. The miniature park contains a bench, a public garden, and a Little Free Library for visitors to explore.
Upper Landing Park is a great place for a stroll along the river, or to sit and watch the river boats go by.
Several picnic tables located throughout the park's open lawns provide a unique riverside experience for residents and visitors traveling along the Mississippi River.
Feronia Square is one of several traffic islands in Saint Paul.
A rather inconspicuous park, Forest Street Triangle utilizes the tip of a larger triangular block to provide passersby with benches and shading.
The St. Clair Recreation Center building has been repartnered with the West 7th Community Center.
Maria Avenue Triangle is decorated with a small garden to beautify the Dayton's Bluff neighborhood. The traffic triangle and avenue takes on the unique pronunciation of "Mariah."

The Rice and Arlington Sports Complex is home to Municipal Athletics' adult softball leagues and a variety of youth baseball and softball games, as well as four indoor batting cages and a large multipurpose room. All fields have lights as well as ample parking for visitors. Field six can also be used for soccer, lacrosse or football.
Located on the Mississippi River, Raspberry Island Regional Park provides stunning views of downtown Saint Paul.
Open green space, playground equipment, and two enclosed tennis courts provide visitors with plenty of ways to stay active or relax at Central Village Park.
Dunning Sports Complex is home to Municipal Athletic adult softball leagues, adult baseball leagues, and a variety of youth softball and baseball events.
This facility has been re-partnered with Joy of the People Soccer Club.
Hidden Falls is located along the Mississippi River and consists of four primary use areas: the primitive area, boat launching area, general picnic area, and scenic falls area.

Webster Park is a popular location for sports among youth residing in the Summit-University neighborhood. Conveniently located behind Obama Elementary School, the park welcomes visitors to play ball and shoot some hoop. A tennis court and practice backboard are also available. An expansive green field also sees plenty of use from football and soccer.

Bordering the Mississippi River just south of the Science Museum of Minnesota, Chestnut Plaza is a beautifully designed public space melding together several serene elements: a modern fountain, warm brick flooring, medium-sized trees, and carved stone benches. Users of the Sam Morgan Regional Trail will find the setting to be a welcome stop.

Formerly referred to as the Fourth and Sibley Tot Lot, Depot Tot Lot received its new name in time for the opening of the nearby Green Line. The name also reflects the transportation theme found throughout the park.
Parque de Castillo contains a tot-lot and many picnic tables for the enjoyment of visitors.
Crosby Farm Regional Park offers beautiful scenery for hiking, biking and fishing.
Parkway Triangles

The award-winning Harriet Island Regional Park is one of Saint Paul's—and one of the Twin Cities'—most popular parks. Located alongside the Mississippi River near downtown Saint Paul, the 'island' boasts many amenities, including the Clarence W. Wigington Pavilion, a 5,000 square foot facility that hosts receptions, parties, weddings, and more throughout the year.
Hillcrest Knoll Park provides the surrounding neighborhood with an accessible, open green space.
Wheelock Parkway Triangles consist of two small, triangular-shaped parks surrounding Wheelock Parkway west of Lake Phalen.
Frogtown Park and Farm is an urban demonstration garden, open space, and natural area currently being developed in the Frogtown neighborhood.
Como Regional Park has one of the widest varieties of free and reasonably priced recreational opportunities in the Twin Cities Metro.
Leroy Triangle is a traffic island near the southwest corner of Como Lake.
Langford Park Recreation Center is home to a wide variety of programs and activities. A large Fourth of July celebration takes place here each year.

Once slated for demolition, the iconic City House is now listed on the National Register of Historic Places. The City House facility, formerly know as the Saint Paul Municipal Elevator and Sackhouse, has been restored as a park pavilion and interpretative center situated on piers and cantilevered out over the Mississippi River.

Cleveland Circle, located at the northwest entrance of the Xcel Energy Center, has three beautiful public gardens and open lawns. The three gardens and lawns occupy their own corners of the busy intersection.

Highland Park offers a wide range of amenities including two golf courses and one disc golf cours, a water park, horseshoe courts, a booya shed, two playgrounds, and extensive picnic areas throughout.
The park is perfect for those looking for a natural escape with views over the nearby backwater lake and downtown Saint Paul skyline.
Lilydale Regional Park, located along the Mississippi River, is currently undergoing restorations and renovations.
Stonebridge Oval is a small traffic circle.
The park's valleys create a distinct feeling of wilderness in conjunction with a bisecting stream that lightly fills the impressive silence and serenity afforded by the environment.
This new nature preserve provides paved bike paths, picnic tables, a restored prairie, and stunning views of Downtown.

Phalen Regional Park is located on beautiful Lake Phalen and is one of Saint Paul's most popular parks. Activities such as fishing, boating, swimming, beach volleyball, festivals, live music, ice skating and x-country skiing keep parkgoers active year round.
Pig's Eye Regional Park is an excellent bird watching area. The park contains one of the largest urban heron and egret rookeries in the Midwest. Many eagles can also be spotted here.

Waḳaƞ Ṭípi is located just east of downtown along the east side of the Mississippi River. The park features 450 million-year-old limestone and sandstone bluffs, spring-fed wetlands, excellent bird watching opportunities, rich Native American history, and beautiful views of the downtown skyline and Mississippi River.
Henry Park is a nature preserve east of Pig's Eye Lake.
The High Bridge Dog Park is a 7-acre, former coal power plant site that was given to the City for operation as a dog-park following clean-up in May 2012.
Mississippi River Gorge Regional Park features several miles of paved trails along the east side of the Mississippi River with beautiful scenic overlooks along the way.
CHS Field will be home to the Saint Paul Saints and the Hamiline Pipers baseball teams.
Prospect Terrace Park provides an unparalleled view of downtown Saint Paul.
Kidd Park sits high atop Saint Paul's bluffs and provides breathtaking views of downtown Saint Paul.

Wic̣aḣapi is arguably the most culturally and historically significant park in Saint Paul. Native American burial mounds approximately 1500-2000 years old sit high on the bluffs, overlooking the Mississippi River and the downtown skyline.
Phalen Recreation Center is located on beautiful Lake Phalen and offers a variety of recreational programs and amenities, including a refrigerated hockey rink in the winter.
With amenities for 13 simultaneous games of horseshoes, this popular location is able to host tournaments, trainings, and casual get-togethers.
The Orchard Recreation Center has been repartnered with Blackhawk Soccer.
Bordering the Soo Line Railroad between 7th Street and the Mississippi River, Bay Triangle makes for an ideal location for small outdoor gatherings.
Southwest of Highland Park, McDonough Park is a large 7-acre preserve densely packed with vegetation.
Parkway
Meeker Island Dog Park Located adjacent to Meeker Island Historic Lock and Dam Site. It feature benches, Off-Leash Dog Park, and Hiking Trail.
Hazel Park Recreation Center offers a wide variety of programs and activities.

Western Sculpture Park is the location of several unique works of art and sculptures created by local artists. Visitors with children will find the large playground area a welcome addition to viewing the works of art scattered throughout the park.
Hamline and Hague Park's main amenity is its circular tot-lot that attracts local families. Visitors will also notice a swinging bench nearby amidst the trees.
A long, thin park dividing Commonwealth Ave.

Aldine Park provides a variety of recreational opportunities for visitors. The park contains a small softball field and a horseshoe area along the park's northern edge. Two playgrounds, a picnic shelter, and a basketball court line the park's southern edge.
Oakland Terrace Park is a one-acre park hugging I-35E to the north at milestone 106.
Parkway
Created during the renovation of Hampden Park, Sydney Triangle functions as a stormwater drain, utilizing runoff water to help new planted bushes and trees flourish.
Prosperity Heights Park is a nearly 10-acre expanse of natural land on Saint Paul's East Side.

Victoria Park is a planned recreational, athletic, and family-friendly space being developed in the West Seventh Neighborhood.
